text:
Payments for AI agents shipped this year. Agents have cards, wallets, rails. Credit didn't. An agent can pay — it still can't borrow, hold a balance sheet, or answer for a loan. That gap is the whole game.

A card is spend-only. It draws down what the agent already has. It can't take a position it settles later, can't be trusted with a limit, can't build. Payments were the easy half.

The hard half is credit: a balance sheet with hard, policy-bounded limits. Borrow against collateral, act autonomously, but never exceed what the policy allows. That's an account, not a card.

Morpho gives agents access to a lending market. Vanna gives them a balance sheet — composable credit rails, for the businesses deploying agents and the agents themselves. One system, both sides. On Stellar testnet.

Building agents that need to borrow, not just spend? This is the credit half. Testnet access is opening to design partners — read the thesis, come build.
